item.title: Researcher reverse engineers Samsung TV firmware, discovers embedded AI listening features [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A security researcher reverse engineered the firmware of a Samsung TV and uncovered that the device contains on-board AI components capable of listening to users. This finding raises concerns about privacy and the extent of AI integration in consumer electronics. The discovery was shared on a public forum, prompting discussions about device security and data handling practices in smart TVs.

item.title: Dessa launches full-duplex conversation AI model trained exclusively on human speech without text data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Dessa, a small AI research lab at Block, has developed a full-duplex speech-to-speech model trained solely on human conversation audio without using text or pretrained models. The model can engage in real-time, natural conversations with emotion, pauses, and nuanced intonation, running locally on high-end MacBook Pro hardware. This approach aims to preserve vocal cues like sarcasm and emotion that are lost when converting speech to text, improving interaction quality and safety in voice AI applications.

item.title: Kimi.ai launches Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed models with 1-million-token context window and improved coding, 3D creation, and financial research capabilities [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Kimi.ai introduced the Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3-trillion parameter open-weight model featuring a 1-million-token context window, and the K3.1 Pro Highspeed variant offering 2-3 times faster performance. These models deliver enhanced capabilities in coding, 3D modeling, and financial workflows, and are available on Kimi.ai platforms with full model weights to be released by November 4. K3.1 Pro improves on its predecessor through extensive post-training and reinforcement learning, achieving competitive scores on coding benchmarks like Terminal-Bench 4.0 and Kimi Code Bench 3.0. It supports complex tasks such as building human walking simulators, creating detailed 3D assets for games and web experiences, and performing multi-step financial data analysis. The models also integrate with tools like Unity, Unreal Engine, Blender, and CAD software to enable advanced agentic and spatial reasoning capabilities.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude AI generated protein candidates for scorpion antivenom but did not invent a working drug, experts say
item.description: An investment research firm, Citrini, collaborated with Anthropic to test whether an unreleased version of the Claude AI model could develop scorpion antivenom. While Claude generated thousands of protein candidates and some showed binding to scorpion toxins, none were proven to neutralize the toxins or function as an effective treatment. The experiment involved designing proteins to bind scorpion venom toxins, with 211 candidates tested by external labs, resulting in 17 proteins binding to four of five targeted toxins. However, experts noted that binding alone does not equate to a viable medicine, and significant challenges remain in translating these findings into a safe and effective antivenom. Citrini acknowledged the limitations of the experiment, and experts cautioned that the results are preliminary and far from a finished drug. The collaboration highlighted both the potential and current limitations of AI in drug discovery, especially in complex biological applications like antivenom development.

item.title: From Software Engineering to AI Research: One Individual's Journey Through 413 Rejections and Academic Challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The article chronicles an individual's transition from a senior software engineering role at Meta in London to pursuing AI research, detailing the numerous rejections faced-metaphorically described as '413 No'-and the persistence required to shift career paths. The author moved from London to Moscow to enroll at Skoltech for a second master's degree, encountering a steep learning curve and initial failures in internships and interviews. The narrative highlights the challenges of adapting to a new field, including rigorous coursework, research work, and overcoming repeated interview rejections at prominent organizations. Despite setbacks, the author gradually identified knowledge gaps and improved through focused study and practical experience, illustrating the difficulties and determination involved in entering AI research from a software engineering background.

item.title: Google DeepMind releases DetectorScope, an AI text detector that explains its predictions with interpretable features and localized evidence [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google DeepMind has released DetectorScope, a tool that detects AI-generated text by breaking down its predictions into named, validated features with descriptions and locations in the text. This approach transforms black-box AI detectors into transparent systems that show which text properties influenced the AI classification and where they appear. DetectorScope uses sparse autoencoders on a language model's residual stream to generate interpretable features, each with a natural-language description and validation score. Users can adjust a threshold parameter to balance interpretability and accuracy, and the tool supports converting existing black-box detectors into auditable ones. DetectorScope maintains performance close to fine-tuned black-box classifiers while providing detailed explanations for its decisions. The tool is available via PyPI and GitHub, includes a demo on Hugging Face, and will be presented at EMNLP 2026 in Budapest. It aims to improve understanding and trust in AI text detection by making the detection process transparent and auditable.

item.title: Glyphh introduces Ada, a decision model that learns from past decisions without using transformers, offering faster and cheaper alternatives to language models [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Glyphh has launched Ada, a decision model designed to replicate past business decisions by learning from historical data rather than generating new reasoning each time like traditional language models. Ada can handle routine decisions independently and escalate uncertain cases to language models, reducing costs and improving consistency. Ada has been benchmarked on tasks such as routing bank messages, credit decisions, and Kubernetes issue classification, demonstrating higher accuracy and significantly lower cost and latency compared to large language models. It records precedents to improve over time and can scale to handle millions of decisions efficiently. Unlike language models, Ada does not generate text or handle novel decisions but excels in repeating established decisions quickly and reliably. Currently in beta, Glyphh plans to expand public benchmarks and develop models capable of answering multiple questions about a case simultaneously.

item.title: Researchers find AI assistance improves short-term task performance but reduces persistence and harms unassisted skills across multiple tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study involving 1,222 participants found that while AI assistance boosts immediate performance in tasks like mathematical reasoning and reading comprehension, it also leads to decreased persistence and worsened performance when individuals work without AI. The researchers suggest that AI's tendency to provide instant answers discourages users from engaging deeply with challenges, which undermines long-term skill development. These findings highlight concerns about cognitive offloading and AI-induced deskilling, emphasizing the need for AI systems to support sustained learning rather than just immediate task completion.

item.title: Study finds Grok AI favors Republican candidates in 92% of midterm races while OpenAI's GPT favors Democrats in 97%, with less than 10% agreement across nearly 500 races [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study tested SpaceXAI's Grok 4.7 and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol by asking each model to recommend a candidate in nearly 500 upcoming midterm election races. Grok recommended Republican candidates 92% of the time, while GPT favored Democrats 97% of the time, with the two models agreeing in fewer than 10% of cases. The study accessed the models via APIs, which differ from consumer chatbot apps that typically avoid direct candidate endorsements. Researchers noted that Grok often cited conservative sources and focused on topics like immigration and taxes, whereas GPT leaned on sources like Wikipedia and the Associated Press and emphasized healthcare and abortion. The study also found that both models showed biases aligned with their recommendations, sometimes ignoring candidates from the opposing party. OpenAI stated that their consumer app is designed to be politically neutral and that the API results do not reflect typical user interactions. The findings highlight potential hidden biases in AI models used for political information, which could influence users' perceptions during elections.

item.title: Analysis confirms AI inference costs drop about 10x annually across multiple benchmarks through 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: An analysis of AI model pricing from 2023 to 2026 confirms that the cost to achieve a given level of AI intelligence has decreased roughly tenfold every year, supporting predictions made by Sam Altman and Kai-Fu Lee. The study examined several benchmarks including Humanity's Last Exam, Arena Elo, GPQA Diamond, and Terminal-Bench, finding consistent cost reductions ranging from 10x every 0.8 to 1.3 years depending on the metric. This rapid decline in AI inference costs, dubbed "Lee's Law," outpaces Moore's Law and suggests AI capabilities are becoming increasingly affordable at an unprecedented rate.

item.title: Discussion questions whether AI is a genuine wealth-building tool or primarily marketed as a get-rich-quick scheme through token sales [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A discussion on Hacker News debates whether AI technology is truly a powerful tool for generating wealth or if it is mainly promoted through selling tokens and books to the public. Commenters argue that if AI were as effective as claimed, developers would focus on building products and forming corporate partnerships, especially in financial markets, rather than selling tokens. The conversation also highlights concerns about AI creating a feedback loop that could degrade the quality of content needed for its own training by displacing the jobs that produce expertise and guidance.

item.title: CoreWeave shares drop nearly 50% amid investor concerns over rising interest rates and heavy debt, despite Nvidia CEO's confidence in neocloud demand [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: CoreWeave's stock has fallen sharply over the past 12 days due to investor worries about the company's ability to manage its substantial debt amid rising interest rates. The decline continued even after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed strong confidence in demand for neocloud services, which CoreWeave provides. Additional market pressures stem from inflation data suggesting further Federal Reserve rate hikes, increasing borrowing costs for debt-dependent companies like CoreWeave. Meanwhile, competitors such as SpaceX are expanding their AI compute offerings with less reliance on debt, intensifying competition in the neocloud market. Meta Platforms' recent announcement of a stock split to raise capital for AI investments also influenced market sentiment, with its shares dropping alongside other neocloud stocks, reflecting broader investor anxiety about the costs and risks associated with AI infrastructure expansion.

item.title: TechCrunch lists notable AI agents that operate via text messages, including Ask Proxy, Caddy, Comma, Fambot, and Folk, serving personal, family, travel, and work needs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A growing number of AI agents now operate directly through text messages, allowing users to complete tasks like scheduling, reminders, research, and reservations without downloading new apps. These agents can remember context, connect to existing services, and proactively assist users across various domains such as personal assistance, family management, and work productivity. Notable examples include Ask Proxy, which anticipates user needs and offers personal and business versions; Caddy, which integrates with messaging platforms to organize scattered information; Comma, an open-source assistant managing tasks across devices; Fambot, designed as a family chief of staff coordinating schedules and communications; and Folk, which runs on a private cloud to execute multi-step tasks. These agents are available on platforms like SMS, iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram, with some in beta and varying pricing models.

item.title: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers deny leaking confidential information and say they were never told what they leaked [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Three former OpenAI safety researchers, Tomek Korbak, Mikita Balesni, and Jasmine Wang, have denied allegations of sharing confidential information following their dismissal and say they were never informed in writing about the specific details of the alleged leaks. They suspect their termination is linked to their advocacy for more transparent AI systems and warn the case could discourage safety concerns being raised within AI companies. OpenAI fired the researchers after an internal investigation into policy violations, citing Signal chats with outside researchers as part of the inquiry but denying that the use of Signal was the reason for the firings. The researchers dispute the official reasoning and highlight concerns about the impact on independent safety audits and internal whistleblowing in the AI industry.

item.title: Block launches Dessa, a full-duplex voice model that runs locally on MacBook M4 Max and mimics human speech with emotion and nuance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Block, led by Jack Dorsey, has developed Dessa, a new voice model that produces highly human-like speech with expressions such as laughs, pauses, and cries. The model runs locally on consumer-grade hardware like the MacBook M4 Max and is trained entirely on human speech using a single NVIDIA GPU. Dessa supports full-duplex communication, allowing it to talk and listen simultaneously, and its conversational knowledge is derived from speech data rather than text input. The company highlights that Dessa's emotional expressiveness is built into the model itself, contrasting with other voice AI systems that rely on text-driven emotion tags. Block has shared examples demonstrating Dessa's ability to convey different emotions and natural cadences during conversations. While the model is not publicly available yet, Block is inviting safety researchers to test it, likely to assess risks related to voice-based deception. This technology could enhance Block's business and consumer offerings by enabling more natural voice interactions at lower costs.

item.title: Rippling shifts majority of coding work from Anthropic to OpenAI models as OpenAI offers lower costs, CEO Parker Conrad says [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI's pricing strategy has led to a significant shift in usage at Rippling, an HR software company. In May, Anthropic's models powered 57% of coding tasks while OpenAI handled 16%, but this reversed to 52% for OpenAI and 18% for Anthropic as the company sought to reduce expenses. CEO Parker Conrad attributed the change to OpenAI's more competitive pricing.

item.title: NBER study finds AI boosts junior patent attorneys' immediate drafting performance but only senior attorneys retain lasting skill gains [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A three-month randomized controlled trial involving 133 patent attorneys across eleven U.S. intellectual property law firms found that AI assistance improved immediate patent drafting performance, especially for junior attorneys with less than seven years of experience. However, when AI was removed, only senior attorneys retained the benefits, suggesting that baseline expertise is necessary to convert AI-assisted work into durable professional skills. The study used an unreleased Google Labs AI assistant called InFlow and measured performance across drafting and redlining tasks. While juniors showed the largest gains during AI-assisted drafting, they did not improve in redlining tasks that require internalized judgment without AI. Researchers observed that senior attorneys restructured drafts based on legal principles, whereas juniors often identified flaws without fixing them, indicating a baseline skill gap that AI did not address. The findings highlight a tension between immediate productivity gains from AI and long-term skill development, which remains critical in professional settings where real-time judgment is required. The study's authors note limitations including sample size, firm representativeness, and the short duration relative to the years needed to build patent expertise, emphasizing the need for further research on AI's impact on professional growth.

item.title: US Air Force seeks AI system to analyze and improve aerial refueling operations using computer vision and machine learning for KC-46 tankers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The US Air Force is soliciting proposals for an AI system to assist aerial refueling crews by automatically analyzing operations from tanker-mounted cameras and providing post-flight feedback. The system aims to measure key metrics such as position, velocity, and alignment during refueling to improve pilot performance, reduce human errors, and enhance mission readiness, focusing initially on the KC-46 tanker platform. The AI solution would generate visual aids like graphic overlays and heat maps to support pilot training and could integrate with virtual reality and simulator systems. This initiative is part of a broader effort to develop scalable AI-enabled aviation performance assessment tools for the Department of Defense, with applications expected to extend beyond the KC-46 to other receiver aircraft types.

item.title: Block launches Dessa, an AI speech model trained solely on human audio to detect emotions and sarcasm in real time, running locally on MacBook Pro M4 Max [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Block, the company behind Square and Cash App, has introduced Dessa, an AI model that processes speech directly as audio without converting it to text. Dessa is designed to recognize emotions, sarcasm, laughter, and pauses in real time and supports full-duplex communication, allowing it to listen and talk simultaneously. The model runs locally on a MacBook Pro M4 Max and was trained on a single NVIDIA GB200 NVL72, but it is not yet publicly available as Block seeks AI security researchers to test it for risks. Previous attempts at emotional voice AI have focused on making voices sound emotionally rich, but Block emphasizes that understanding emotional cues directly from speech can improve human-AI communication and safety. Dessa was developed out of curiosity and a desire for better interaction, distinguishing it from other voice AI systems that rely on text-based processing or focus mainly on voice synthesis quality.

item.title: Calm Company Fund used AI to resolve a two-year lawsuit favorably, overcoming high legal costs and systemic challenges in Delaware courts
item.description: Calm Company Fund faced a challenging two-year lawsuit that threatened significant financial and emotional strain. The company leveraged AI tools to effectively manage the legal process and counter well-funded opponents, ultimately achieving a favorable resolution. The article explains the difficulties defendants face in the Delaware legal system, including the high costs of discovery and the limited chances of early dismissal under the "American Rule." It details how AI helped the company navigate these hurdles, providing strategic advantages despite the system's bias toward plaintiffs. This experience offers lessons for entrepreneurs with limited legal budgets facing similar litigation risks.

item.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today - it's not yet open weights, but Moonshot promise "Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026". They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same). The US dollar pricing is $2.00/million tokens for input and $10/million for output - the same as GPT-6.1 Sol and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5. Moonshot's own benchmarks show Kimi as approximately level with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra - beating them on a few benchmarks, coming close on others. Artificial Analysis scored Kimi at 55 - ahead of Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon (all at 53) and behind only Claude Opus 5.5 (58). This is the first time a (soon-to-be) open weight model has scored this highly against the frontier. I tried it out via the Moonshot API using the llm openai endpoint command I added to LLM 0.32 back in August: llm openai endpoint \ https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 \ --key kimi \ -m kimi-k3.1-pro \ "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" \ --responses \ -o reasoning_effort low \ > kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stdout.txt \ 2> kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stderr.txt llm openai endpoint can run prompts against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint but doesn't log the results, hence the extra options to save stdout and stderr (the reasoning trace). Here are the pelicans I got for Kimi K3.1 Pro on the three reasoning levels it supports - low, medium, and max. This is max: For comparison, I ran fresh pelicans against Kimi K3 on those three reasoning levels. Via Hacker News Tags: ai, generative-ai, llms, llm, llm-pricing, pelican-riding-a-bicycle, llm-release, ai-in-china, moonshot, kimi

item.title: VC Firms Tap LP Pools, Warehouse Loans for Speedy AI Cash [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: When Reflection AI set out to raise $2.5 billion early this year, one of its existing venture backers, B Capital, was eager to invest again in the startup, which has emerged as the most high-profile U.S. maker of open-source AI models. But Reflection's valuation had more than tripled in just six months, forcing investors to write big checks for a sizable stake. Such a check would have been too big for B Capital's main venture fund, a $500 million vehicle raised in July. To come up with the cash, the company turned to a different source of capital: a pool of money apart from its regular fund, designed to give limited partners-the pension funds, endowments and wealthy individuals that back VC firms-more direct access to hot startups like Reflection at reduced fees.

item.title: Article: Multi-Cloud FinOps: An Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
item.description: Multi-cloud flexibility comes with hidden egress costs driven by service placement and communication patterns. item.title: Anthropic's Elevator Problem: Persuading Investors to Share Its AI Dream [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: One quotation has rattled around in my head for a while, which I first heard from early Anthropic investor Jaan Tallinn: "The future of the world will be decided by a group of people who fit in an elevator." The enigmatic billionaire said on a podcast earlier this year that a friend had used the illustration to describe the concentration of power at the leading AI companies. I've been reflecting on it as Anthropic prepares for its Wall Street debut because the company's small group of powerful insiders, who are set to realize incredible wealth at unprecedented speed, face their biggest test in explaining themselves to the world outside their elevator. To raise the money Anthropic leaders need, and to keep raising it again and again, big fund managers need to fully buy in.
